title: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) - Consumer Rights Manual
content:
## 1. Statutory Warranty and Defective Goods in Dubai
Under Dubai Consumer Protection guidelines and UAE Federal Law:
- All household appliances, including air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, and electronic goods, carry a mandatory legal warranty from the authorized dealer or retailer of at least one (1) to two (2) years.
- If an appliance fails or exhibits a major manufacturing defect within fourteen (14) days from the date of purchase or installation, the consumer is legally entitled to:
  1. An immediate replacement with a brand new unit of identical specifications, or
  2. A complete full refund of the purchase price without deduction, returned using the original payment method.
- If a defect occurs after fourteen (14) days but within the warranty period:
  - The supplier is obligated to repair the defective item free of charge.
  - Repairs must not exceed fifteen (15) to twenty-one (21) calendar days.
  - If parts are unavailable or the repair cannot be completed within 21 days, or if the unit suffers the same defect three (3) consecutive times, the merchant must replace the unit or issue a full refund.
  - The merchant must provide a temporary loaner replacement for essential appliances (such as air conditioners in summer or refrigerators) during extended repairs.

title: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) - Consumer Rights Manual
content:
## 2. Invoices and Proof of Purchase
- Merchants in Dubai are legally mandated to issue bilingual (Arabic and English) tax invoices for every commercial transaction.
- The invoice must state the merchant trade name, date of purchase, invoice number, itemized description, quantities, unit price, VAT breakdown, and return/warranty conditions.
- Failure of a merchant to issue an official invoice is a regulatory violation subject to administrative fines.

authority: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism
jurisdiction: Dubai Emirate (Commercial entities, retail stores, local e-commerce, home appliances, automotive, electronics)
title: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) - Consumer Rights Manual
content:
## 3. Delayed Delivery and Non-Performance
- When a delivery date is agreed upon (verbal or written), the supplier must fulfill delivery within the stipulated window.
- In case of a merchant delay exceeding seven (7) days without consumer consent:
  - The consumer has the legal right to cancel the purchase agreement and receive a full immediate refund.
  - The supplier cannot impose cancellation or restocking penalties when the delay was caused by the merchant.

title: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET) - Consumer Rights Manual
content:
## 4. Misleading Advertising and Pricing Discrepancies
- The displayed price on shelf, website, or promotional flyer must match the price charged at checkout.
- If a discrepancy exists, the merchant is legally bound to honor the lower displayed price.
- Misleading promotions, fake discounts, and bait-and-switch advertising are strictly prohibited under Article 17 of UAE Law.

content:
## 5. Official Complaint Filing Procedure in Dubai
- **Step 1: Direct Merchant Escalation**: The consumer should first submit a formal written complaint (via email, customer service ticket, or registered message) to the merchant, giving a 7-day cure window.
- **Step 2: Filing with Dubai DED (Consumer Rights)**: If the merchant is unresponsive or refuses resolution:
  - Portal: https://consumerrights.gov.ae/en/Pages/consumer-complaint.aspx
  - Dubai Consumer Smart App (iOS / Android)
  - Toll-free Helpline: 600 545555
- **Required Documents**:
  1. Copy of the Tax Invoice / Receipt.
  2. Copy of Warranty Certificate / Card.
  3. Evidence of communication with merchant (emails, chat logs, call reference numbers).
  4. Photographs or video documentation showing the defect or model serial number.
  5. Emirates ID or Resident Passport copy of the complainant.
- **Resolution Timeline**: Dubai DED initiates mediation within four (4) business days and resolves typical retail disputes within seven (7) to fourteen (14) business days.

title: Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism - Merchant Standards & Consumer Protection Blue Book
content:
## Consumer Protection Standards for Commercial Outlets
1. **Mandatory Bilingual Receipt**:
   Every merchant operating in Dubai must issue a receipt printed in Arabic and English. The receipt must clearly state the merchant's trade name, TRN, date, item, price in UAE Dirhams (AED), and store return/exchange policy.
2. **"No Return, No Exchange" Clauses Prohibited**:
   Clauses stating "Goods once sold cannot be returned or exchanged" are legally null and void if the good is found to be defective, counterfeit, non-conforming to technical standards, or unfit for purpose.
3. **Air Conditioning & Home Appliance Specific Standards**:
   - Authorized dealers must provide manufacturer warranty cards stamped with purchase date.
   - For air conditioning units installed by the retailer or certified technician, warranty covers compressor for five (5) years and full unit parts/labor for minimum two (2) years.
   - If an air conditioning unit ceases cooling or leaks refrigerant within 14 days of installation due to manufacturing or certified installation error, dealer must replace unit within 7 business days or refund in full.
4. **Resolution Deadlines**:
   - Merchants must respond to formal customer service complaints within 48 hours.
   - If the merchant fails to reach an amicable settlement, the consumer may submit case to Dubai Consumer Rights CCCP.

authority: Ministry of Economy, United Arab Emirates
title: UAE Federal Law No. 15 of 2020 on Consumer Protection & Executive Regulations
content:
## Legislative Overview
Federal Law No. 15 of 2020 replaced the earlier Federal Law No. 24 of 2006, expanding statutory protections to cover electronic commerce, digital services, data privacy, fair contract terms, and rapid dispute settlement. The Executive Regulations enacted under Cabinet Decision No. 66 of 2023 set enforceable operational rules across all retail and service sectors in the United Arab Emirates.

authority: Ministry of Economy, United Arab Emirates
title: UAE Federal Law No. 15 of 2020 on Consumer Protection & Executive Regulations
content:
## Article 4 & 5: Fundamental Consumer Rights
1. Right to Safety: Protection against products, production processes, and services that endanger consumer health or safety.
2. Right to Knowledge: Right to receive accurate, transparent, and complete information regarding goods and services, including genuine country of origin, specifications, operating manuals, and clear pricing in AED.
3. Right to Redress and Fair Compensation: Right to prompt settlement of legitimate claims, repair of defective items, replacement, or restitution of financial damages resulting from defective or substandard goods.

authority: Ministry of Economy, United Arab Emirates
title: UAE Federal Law No. 15 of 2020 on Consumer Protection & Executive Regulations
content:
## Article 10: Defective Goods, Malfunctions, and Supplier Liability
- The supplier is legally liable for any manufacturing defect, lack of conformity, or performance failure that renders the good unfit for its customary use.
- Upon discovery of a defect within the statutory warranty or reasonable operational lifetime:
  1. The consumer has the legal right to demand the repair of the good, replacement with an identical or superior compliant good, or return of the purchase price against return of the defective item.
  2. If the defect is fundamental, critical to safety, or cannot be repaired within the regulatory period (maximum 14 to 21 calendar days), the supplier must issue an immediate refund or replacement without charging depreciation.

authority: Ministry of Economy, United Arab Emirates
title: UAE Federal Law No. 15 of 2020 on Consumer Protection & Executive Regulations
content:
## Article 12: Warranty Obligations and After-Sales Maintenance
- Suppliers, distributors, and agents are legally obliged to provide after-sales servicing, warranty repairs, and periodic maintenance throughout the expected economic lifetime of the product.
- Mandatory spare parts must be stocked for consumer durables (vehicles, air conditioners, major electrical appliances) by authorized distributors for a minimum of 5 years or the product life cycle.

authority: Ministry of Economy, United Arab Emirates
title: UAE Federal Law No. 15 of 2020 on Consumer Protection & Executive Regulations
content:
## Article 17: Prohibited Deceptive Commercial Conduct
- Advertising or packaging containing fraudulent, exaggerated, or misleading claims is prohibited.
- Hidden costs, compulsory bundling of unwanted auxiliary warranties without affirmative consumer consent, and unilateral alterations of agreed terms are unlawful.

authority: Ministry of Economy, United Arab Emirates
title: UAE Federal Law No. 15 of 2020 on Consumer Protection & Executive Regulations
content:
## Article 25: Penalties for Non-Compliance
- Failure to comply with consumer protection directives or refusing lawful refunds exposes the offending merchant to administrative fines ranging from AED 10,000 up to AED 1,000,000, temporary license suspension, or business closure ordered by the competent authority.

content:
## Statutory Consumer Dispute Jurisdiction Matrix
Filing with the correct government body ensures immediate jurisdiction and avoids administrative rejection.

### 1. Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism (DET / DED)
- **Scope**: Commercial purchases, retail stores, local service providers, restaurants, supermarkets, home appliances (ACs, electronics), Dubai-licensed e-commerce vendors.
- **Authority**: Commercial Compliance & Consumer Protection (CCCP).
- **Portal**: https://consumerrights.gov.ae/
- **Contact**: 600 545555.

### 2. UAE Ministry of Economy (MOEC)
- **Scope**: Cross-emirate commercial disputes, national anti-monopoly violations, pricing disputes on basic food commodities, businesses operating without emirate-level consumer bureaus.
- **Portal**: https://www.moec.gov.ae/en/consumer-protection
- **Contact**: 800 1222.

### 3. Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA)
- **Scope**: Mobile network operators (e& / Etisalat, du, Virgin Mobile UAE), fixed broadband, cellular contract billing, sim swaps, data bundle disputes, postal delivery services (Emirates Post).
- **Condition**: Consumer must first obtain a formal complaint reference number from the telecom provider and wait five (5) working days before escalating to TDRA.
- **Portal**: https://tdra.gov.ae/en/services/consumer-complaints
- **Contact**: 800 12.

### 4. Sanadak - Financial & Insurance Ombudsman (Central Bank of UAE)
- **Scope**: Commercial banks, Islamic financial institutions, insurance companies, credit card unauthorized debits, mortgage disputes, consumer credit claims.
- **Eligibility**: Independent Ombudsman established by federal decree to deliver binding rulings up to statutory limits.
- **Portal**: https://sanadak.gov.ae/
- **Contact**: 800 7262325 (800 SANADAK).

### 5. Dubai Land Department (DLD / RERA)
- **Scope**: Real estate tenant-landlord disputes, property developer maintenance escrow, rental increases contrary to the RERA calculator.
- **Portal**: https://dubailand.gov.ae/

content:
## Consumer Redress Checklist
1. Purchase Proof: Valid Tax Invoice indicating TRN (Tax Registration Number) and merchant name.
2. Timeline of Incident: Documenting date of purchase, date of failure, and merchant notification date.
3. Merchant Response Record: Copies of emails, support tickets, or registered SMS notices.
4. Objective Redress Specification: Clearly stating whether requesting repair, replacement, or refund.
